subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as an onboarding/provider auth method, and what scopes, callback, token-storage, refresh, billing/account detection, and fallback contract are acceptable?
rationale: Source inspection shows the helper exists but the provider deliberately does not expose it as an auth choice; choosing to make it one-click onboarding crosses credential-security and first-run product boundaries that automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve Additive OAuth Method
options.body: Expose a provider-owned Anthropic OAuth method after maintainers approve the security, billing, docs, migration, and fallback contract while preserving existing setup paths.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Continue supporting API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI setup, and reduce friction with copy/docs or detection improvements instead of browser OAuth.

options.title: Prototype Behind Experimental UX
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth path that is not the default until live provider and security proof are strong.

recommendation.title: Approve Additive OAuth Method
recommendation.body: Expose a provider-owned Anthropic OAuth method after maintainers approve the security, billing, docs, migration, and fallback contract while preserving existing setup paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal for Anthropic auth/onboarding decisions points to steipete's provider-auth and setup-choice work.
